story.head: The Sabres come in rested
paras: The Blue Jackets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-3 in Columbus on Oct 1. The Sabres have won three straight, while the Blue Jackets (5-7-0) lost 3-1 to Dallas on Saturday. The Blue Jackets played last night, and the Sabres are rested. Going in, the Blue Jackets are last in the Metropolitan (tied for 29th in the NHL) and the Sabres seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 13th).

The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.417) says: their chances are worth about .482, and their finishing has held them back. The Sabres’ record (.607) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.540), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (5th), keep things calm after the whistle (5th lowest) and have a leaky penalty kill (30th). Columbus has scored 2.33 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd), but don't block many shots (29th). The Jackets have the edge over the Sabres on forecheck pressure.

Kent Johnson (7 G / 5 A / 12 P in 12 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Zach Werenski (0 G / 10 A / 10 P in 12 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (10 G / 7 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 14 GP) is next in line.

Cam Talbot (3-2-0 / .893 SV% in 5 GS) will likely start for Columbus. Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (4-3-3 / .873 SV% in 9 GS) and Colten Ellis (3-1-0 / .880 SV% in 5 GS). Luukkonen has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Saturday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
